sections.overview: The common name White-vented Violetear refers to this hummingbird’s violet ear patch and pale lower belly.
sections.identification: Males are green with violet ear patches and bluish-violet chest tones; females are duller and lack the violet patch.
sections.habitat: It uses semi-open scrub, savanna, grassland, bushy ravines and forest edges across central South America.
sections.diet: It takes nectar from flowers and supplements it with small arthropods, which provide animal protein.
sections.behavior: It is territorial around flower patches and may move locally between highlands and valleys with seasonal conditions.
sections.reproduction: The female builds a small cup nest and usually lays one or two eggs; she incubates while the male brings food.
sections.ecology: The genus also includes other violetears, such as Colibri coruscans. The pale vent is a useful field mark for this species.
sections.conservation: The cited species account lists it as Least Concern, though local habitat conditions vary across its wide range.
